Description: {Benefit} for {Target User} — 6-12 words max. Specific outcome > generic promise.
Do: 'Build stunning UIs in minutes not hours'
Example_Good: 'Ship 10x faster with production-ready React components' — specific benefit + target
Example_Bad: 'Welcome to our amazing platform' — generic no value prop

Description: Clarifies the headline. HOW you deliver the benefit. 1 sentence max.
Dont: 'We provide comprehensive solutions for your needs'
Example_Good: '206 developers from 11 countries trust EaseUI to ship faster' — social proof subhead
Example_Bad: 'Our industry-leading solutions leverage cutting-edge technology' — buzzword soup

Description: Action Verb + Outcome. Not 'Sign Up' — 'Start Building Free'. Contrasting color.
Example_Bad: Gray button: 'Submit' — no motivation zero context

Description: Numbers + credibility. '206 devs from 11 countries' > 'Trusted by developers'.
Do: Show specific numbers: users signups countries
Dont: 'Trusted by thousands' (vague) or no social proof at all
Example_Good: '4.9★ rating • 3M+ downloads • Used in 15 countries' — specific credible
Example_Bad: 'Best rated app' — no evidence no specifics

Description: 3 bullet points of pain your audience feels. Use THEIR words not yours.
Do: Use exact phrases from customer interviews
Example_Good: 'Tired of building the same button component for every project?' — emotional real
Example_Bad: 'Our platform addresses suboptimal workflow inefficiencies' — robot speak

Description: Show (don't tell) how your product solves the problem. Screenshot or demo GIF.
Do: Product screenshot in context with annotation
Example_Good: GIF showing: click component → copy code → paste in project → beautiful result
Example_Bad: 'Our solution leverages AI-powered algorithms' — no visual proof

Description: Top 3 features ONLY. Each with benefit not feature name. Feature + So What?
Do: 'Dark mode support — ship accessible UIs without extra work'
Dont: List 15 features with technical names nobody understands
Example_Good: 3 cards: Speed (ship 10x faster) + Quality (production-ready) + Flexibility (customize everything)
Example_Bad: Feature matrix with 50 checkmarks comparing 8 competitors

Description: 3 tiers max. Highlight recommended plan. Show annual savings. Include free tier.
Do: Clear pricing with obvious recommended choice
Dont: Hidden pricing or 'Contact sales' for a $19 product
Example_Good: Free / Pro $19/mo / Team $49/seat — with 'Most Popular' badge on Pro
Example_Bad: 'Custom pricing — schedule a demo' for a simple SaaS = kills conversion

Description: Answer top 5 objections. Not generic FAQs — real concerns your audience has.
Do: 'Can I use EaseUI components in commercial projects? Yes, MIT licensed.'
Dont: 'What is EaseUI? EaseUI is a...' (they already know this if they're on your page)
Example_Good: Objection-based: 'Is it better than shadcn/ui?' with honest answer
Example_Bad: Generic FAQ that doesn't address real buying concerns

Description: Repeat the main CTA. Add urgency or reminder of value. Different angle.
Dont: Same exact CTA as top without any new motivation
Example_Good: 'Still here? Your next project deserves better components. Start free →'
Example_Bad: 'Sign up' (same button same text as hero = no motivation to scroll-to-CTA)

Description: < 2 seconds load time. Compress images. Minimize JS. LCP < 2.5s.
Do: Test with Lighthouse. Target 90+ performance score
Dont: Heavy animations or unoptimized images that slow load > 3s
Example_Good: LCP 1.2s — hero image optimized WebP — JS deferred
Example_Bad: 15 animated sections + uncompressed PNGs → 8s load → 50% bounce

Description: 60%+ traffic is mobile. Test on real phone not just browser resize.
Do: Design mobile-first then scale up to desktop
Dont: Build desktop-only and 'make it responsive later'
Example_Good: Mobile: stacked layout single-column CTA full-width easy thumb reach
Example_Bad: Desktop layout shrunk to mobile — tiny text unclickable buttons
